title: LLM Logbook Schema (General Projects)
description: Schema for tracking context across sessions in non-software projects (academic, creative, business, other). Supports long-term memory, objective tracking with actionable guidance, and progress documentation.
$comment: CANONICAL SHAPE (read this if you forked or adopted mid-flight): the logbook is an object with exactly these top-level keys — ticket, objectives, recent_context, history_summary, future_reminders, governance_context. 'objectives' has 'main' and 'secondary', each an ARRAY of objects with integer id. There is NO 'meta', 'context', 'completed_at', 'notes', or 'ui_requirements' top-level field. If you find yourself wanting to add an undeclared sibling field, that is the signal you are putting content in the wrong artifact — re-read where it belongs (strategy → roadmap; the what+why of a deliverable → objectives; running progress → recent_context).

ticket.description: Metadata of the task, milestone, or deliverable that anchors this logbook. This is the ultimate goal that all objectives contribute to.
ticket.$comment: Populate from user input. Title and description are required. URL is optional (link to project management tool, shared document, etc.).

title.description: Title of the task, milestone, or deliverable. Should be concise and descriptive.
title.$comment: Ask user for clear title. Keep under 100 characters.

url.description: URL to related resource (project management tool, shared document, reference material).
url.$comment: Optional. Leave empty string if no external resource. Examples: Notion page, Google Doc, Trello card.

external_ref.description: Structured reference to the task in an external tracker, when a plain url is insufficient (e.g. an Asana task id, a Notion database row).
external_ref.$comment: Optional. Officializes the external-id field adopters invented. STOP: one external system per logbook; if the work spans two trackers, that is two logbooks. REDIRECT: the human link goes in `url`; the task prose in `description`; do NOT add system-specific custom keys here. `system` is a free string (no closed enum — validating a specific tracker is the command's job, not the schema's). bad: {'asana_id': 'X', 'notion': 'Y'} (two systems + custom keys). good: {'system': 'asana', 'id': '1203...', 'url': 'https://...'}.

system.description: Name of the external tracker (free string), e.g. 'asana', 'notion', 'trello'.

id.description: Identifier of the item within that system.

url.description: Direct link to the item (may duplicate ticket.url).

ui_requirements.description: UI/visual scope of the task, when it involves a visual deliverable. Optional. Officializes the field logbook-create Step 2.1 already emits.
ui_requirements.$comment: Optional. STOP: describe visual SCOPE only — whether there is a visual deliverable, the references, brief notes. REDIRECT: the production steps go in the secondaries' completion_guide; design rationale -> a decision or the brief; do NOT paste full specs here. bad: the entire brand-guideline text. good: {has_ui: true, visual_references: ['brief.pdf'], notes: 'follow brand palette v2'}.

has_ui.description: True if the task involves a visual/UI deliverable.

visual_references.description: Paths or URLs to mocks, references, examples.

notes.description: Brief notes on the visual requirements.

description.description: Detailed explanation of what needs to be accomplished. Includes acceptance criteria, deadlines, or constraints if available.
description.$comment: GOAL + ACCEPTANCE in 2-4 sentences (~600 chars is plenty). State the deliverable and how you will know it is done. This ANCHORS the work — it is not a design doc, a step list, or a planning dump. REDIRECT: how to do it (that is each secondary's completion_guide), the why behind each objective (that is main_objective.context), running progress (that is recent_context). bad: a 1500-char essay listing every section, every stakeholder email, the full methodology, and a phase-by-phase plan → good: 'Publish the Q3 market-entry report. Done when the 12-page report is delivered to the board with all 4 required sections (market size, competitors, pricing, risks) and approved in the Jun 30 review.'

objectives.description: Project objectives organized by priority. Main objectives define high-level deliverables. Secondary objectives are actionable steps with guidance.
objectives.$comment: Main objectives provide context and references. Secondary objectives provide step-by-step guidance. Both can be populated together.

main.description: Primary objectives that define major deliverables or milestones.
main.$comment: Each main objective should have clear context and reference materials. For academic: chapters, papers. For creative: assets, deliverables. For business: milestones, documents.

secondary.description: Actionable objectives that contribute to main objectives. Each contains specific guidance for completion.
secondary.$comment: Break down main objectives into completable steps. Provide guidance referencing documents, examples, standards, or best practices.

recent_context.description: Running log of recent interactions, findings, decisions, and progress. Newest entries at index 0. Sliding window that compacts to history_summary when full.
recent_context.$comment: Prepend new entries at index 0. When array exceeds maxItems, remove last (oldest) entry and summarize it to history_summary. Never replace entire array.

items.description: Single context entry representing a meaningful interaction, finding, or decision.
items.$comment: Create entry for: progress updates, important findings, decisions made, blockers encountered, feedback received. Keep content focused and actionable.

id.description: Unique identifier for this entry. Immutable once created.
id.$comment: Start at 1, increment by 1 globally across all entries. Never reuse IDs.

created_at.description: UTC timestamp when entry was created (ISO 8601). Immutable.
created_at.$comment: Set once at creation. Never modify.

content.description: Entry content describing action, decision, finding, or progress. Should be meaningful and provide context for future sessions.
content.$comment: Write concisely but completely. Include: what happened, why it matters, any decisions made. Future sessions will use this to understand context.

mood.description: User's emotional state during this entry if observable (focused, frustrated, excited, uncertain, overwhelmed).
mood.$comment: Optional. Only populate if user mood is clearly observable. Helps adjust communication style.

history_summary.description: Compact summaries of entries removed from recent_context. Preserves continuity when short-term memory is full. Newest at index 0.
history_summary.$comment: Write here ONLY when truncating recent_context. Summarize removed entry in max 140 chars. Prepend at index 0. If exceeds maxItems, remove oldest (last) entry.

items.description: Compressed summary of a removed recent_context entry.
items.$comment: Capture essential information only: what was done, key decision, or important finding.

id.description: Unique identifier for this summary. Immutable once created.
id.$comment: Start at 1, increment by 1. Separate sequence from recent_context IDs.

created_at.description: UTC timestamp when summary was created (ISO 8601). Immutable.
created_at.$comment: Set once at creation. Never modify.

content.description: Compressed summary of removed entry. Must capture essential information.
content.$comment: Summarize in tweet-length. Focus on: what was done, outcome, or key decision.

mood.description: User's emotional state at time of original entry if it was recorded.
mood.$comment: Optional. Preserve from original entry if present.

future_reminders.description: User-created reminders for future sessions. Agent surfaces these when their time arrives.
future_reminders.$comment: Only add reminders when user explicitly requests. Check this array at session start and surface any due reminders.

items.description: A scheduled reminder to surface in a future session.
items.$comment: Create only on explicit user request. Remove after surfacing to user.

id.description: Unique identifier for this reminder. Immutable once created.
id.$comment: Start at 1, increment by 1. Never reuse IDs.

created_at.description: UTC timestamp when reminder was created (ISO 8601). Immutable.
created_at.$comment: Set once at creation. Never modify.

content.description: Reminder message to surface to user when due.
content.$comment: Write exactly what user wants to be reminded about. Include any context needed.

when.description: UTC timestamp when this reminder should be surfaced to user.
when.$comment: Compare against current time at session start. Surface if current time >= when.

governance_context.description: Compact extracted subset of the blueprint chain (scope → product → company) that impacts this logbook's direction. Same shape as logbook_software_schema.governance_context (cross-schema consistency).
governance_context.$comment: Populated by logbook-create A1.4 via deterministic jq queries against each blueprint in the parent_blueprint chain. Loaded into objectives-implement Step 5 'Governance banner' so implementers carry blueprint-level alignment without re-reading full blueprints. Forward-only: pre-existing logbooks without this field continue to validate; new logbooks populate it.

main_objective.description: High-level objective defining a major deliverable or milestone. Provides context and reference materials for deeper work.
main_objective.$comment: Define clear outcomes with supporting context. References can be documents, URLs, assets, or any relevant materials. Standards can be style guides, regulations, methodologies, or best practices.

id.description: Unique identifier for this main objective. Immutable once created.
id.$comment: Start at 1, increment by 1. Never reuse IDs even after abandonment.

created_at.description: UTC timestamp when objective was created (ISO 8601). Immutable.
created_at.$comment: Set once at creation. Never modify.

content.description: Verifiable outcome statement that serves as acceptance criteria. When this statement is true, the objective is achieved.
content.$comment: ONE verifiable outcome per objective. STOP: if the text contains '+', 'y'/'and', an em-dash, a colon-list, or two verbs, it is multi-concern — split it into separate objectives. Write as outcome, not task; ask 'can I clearly say yes/no this is done?'. REDIRECT: the design choice or method (→ main_objective.context for the why, the secondary's completion_guide for the how); a second deliverable (→ a second objective); how you will prove it (→ verification_demonstrations). bad: 'Draft chapter 2 AND get advisor approval AND format citations in APA' (3 concerns) → good: 'Chapter 2 draft completed and approved by advisor' (one outcome; APA formatting and the approval check become their own objectives/demonstrations).

context.description: Rationale and background: who needs this, what problem it solves, deadlines, dependencies, or constraints.
context.$comment: The WHY only — who needs this, what constraint or deadline forces the approach. STOP: keep it to the rationale; the moment you write a verb-of-action ('write', 'send', 'format') you have drifted into how. REDIRECT: implementation steps (→ the secondary's completion_guide); planning-process labels like 'Dimensión N', 'Mindset:', 'orthogonality_review' (those are planning scratch, not durable context — never persist them); re-listing the materials/standards already in scope.references / scope.standards. Test: remove every proper noun and label — if no 'why' sentence remains, you wrote 'how' in the wrong field. bad: 'Dimensión 2 / Mindset: rigor. Apply APA per scope.standards, see Chapter 1 draft, then write section by section' → good: 'The dissertation committee requires chapter 2 before the Jul 15 defense scheduling deadline; it depends on the approved chapter 1 framing.'

scope.description: Boundaries for this objective: reference materials and standards/guidelines to follow.
scope.$comment: References are starting points (documents, URLs, assets, examples). Standards are guidelines (style guides, regulations, methodologies, best practices).

references.description: Reference materials for this objective: documents, URLs, assets, examples, or prior work to build upon.
references.$comment: List relevant materials. Examples: 'Chapter 2 draft in Google Docs', 'Competitor analysis PDF', 'Brand guidelines v2', 'client_feedback_notes.md', 'https://example.com/reference'.

standards.description: Guidelines, standards, or methodologies to follow. Empty array if none defined.
standards.$comment: List applicable standards. Examples: 'APA 7th edition citation format', 'Brand voice guidelines', 'ISO 27001 compliance', 'Lean Canvas methodology'.

status.description: Current state: not_started (pending work), active (in progress), blocked (waiting on external input), achieved (completed), abandoned (cancelled).
status.$comment: Set only ONE main objective as 'active' at a time. Use 'blocked' when waiting for feedback, resources, or dependencies. Set 'achieved' ONLY when content statement is verified true AND all entries in verification_demonstrations have verdict='pass' (design_principle #8 — see field $comment for protocol). For general projects in w4: verification_demonstrations is build-forward-compatible (taxonomy declared, evidence-critic opt-in via verification rule).

verification_demonstrations.description: Observable executable evidence that this primary outcome was achieved. Required on every NEW primary (forward-only per blueprint decision #15). Status='achieved' requires verdict='pass' on every entry. Empty/absent only on grandfathered historical logbooks. For general projects: forward-compatible — evidence-critic is opt-in via verification rule (decision #6 w4 roadmap).
verification_demonstrations.$comment: design_principle #8 (Demonstration over declaration). PROTOCOL (logbook-create Phase 4 w4): A4.5 verification-designer (fresh subagent, blocking) proposes type-aware demonstrations per primary based on scope.references + standards + content keywords. A4.6 feasibility-checker (fresh subagent, blocking) verifies that required resources (documents, tools, reviewers) are accessible; if missing, A4 inserts provisioning secondaries BEFORE work begins. Both subagents UNCONDITIONAL. General-project type lens (Phase 3.4 w4): evidence-critic OPT-IN via verification rule — for academic/creative/business primaries, types like external_observation (peer review, stakeholder approval), documentation_consistency (deliverable matches spec), behavior_check (assert the artifact does what it claims) are typical; software-only types (unit_test/integration_test) can still be selected if the primary touches code-adjacent deliverables. Bootstrap forward-compatible: general projects build with the field structurally even if validation tooling matures in later waves. DRY with test_cases (product_rule #10): when a primary's secondaries declared test_cases, the demonstration REFERENCES the suite covering them ('suite covering these cases passes, verdict=pass') and does NOT re-enumerate — test_cases SPECIFY (design), verification_demonstrations PROVE (achievement). Enumerate once, prove once.

items.description: Single verification demonstration: one observable check tied to an acceptance criterion of the primary.
items.$comment: Each entry binds a verification TYPE to a concrete TARGET and an EXPECTED observable outcome. command_or_method describes how to execute (file inspection, reviewer call, deterministic command). verdict='pending' until executed; flip to 'pass' or 'fail' with evidence.

type.description: Verification taxonomy (10 types — shared across project types). General-leaning: external_observation (peer/stakeholder review), documentation_consistency (deliverable vs spec/standard), behavior_check (artifact does what it claims), adversarial_review (fresh-subagent critique). Software-only types remain available for code-adjacent general primaries.
type.$comment: A4.5 verification-designer infers type from primary's scope.references + standards + content keywords. General patterns: paper/manuscript → external_observation (reviewer) + documentation_consistency (style guide); design assets → external_observation (stakeholder approval) + behavior_check (asset renders/responds as described); business plan/strategy → documentation_consistency (vs methodology) + adversarial_review (fresh critic).

target.description: Concrete artifact being verified — document path/URL, deliverable name, asset identifier, reviewer/stakeholder role.
target.$comment: Reference the actual artifact. Examples: 'Chapter 2 manuscript v3 (Google Doc URL)', 'Brand identity package final v2', 'Q3 marketing plan section 4'.

expected.description: Observable outcome that proves the demonstration passes. Must be checkable, bound to an acceptance criterion.
expected.$comment: Concrete, not aspirational. Examples: 'reviewer signs approval form', 'APA style checker reports 0 violations', 'stakeholder approval recorded in meeting notes dated YYYY-MM-DD', 'critic verdict in [confirmed, gold]'. Avoid 'looks good', 'feels right'.

command_or_method.description: How this demonstration is executed: deterministic command, reviewer/stakeholder invocation, file inspection method, or subagent prompt.
command_or_method.$comment: Examples: 'send to advisor for review (deadline: 3 days)', 'run APA-style checker over chapter PDF', 'evidence-critic subagent reviews substance vs claim', 'compare deliverable section 4 against brand guidelines v2'.

verdict.description: Execution outcome. status='achieved' on the primary REQUIRES verdict='pass' on ALL entries.
verdict.$comment: Stays 'pending' until verification runs. Flip to 'pass' when expected matches observed; 'fail' otherwise with reason in evidence. NEVER leave 'pending' when marking primary as achieved.

verified_at.description: UTC ISO 8601 timestamp when verdict was recorded. Absent while verdict='pending'.
verified_at.$comment: Set ONCE when verdict flips from 'pending'. Immutable after.

evidence.description: Observable proof supporting the verdict: reviewer sign-off snippet, checker output, stakeholder approval reference, subagent classification.
evidence.$comment: Concrete and auditable. Examples for pass: 'advisor approval email dated 2026-06-10', 'APA checker: 0 violations on 24 pages', 'critic verdict=confirmed'. For fail: reason + counter-evidence. Required when verdict != 'pending'.

secondary_objective.description: Actionable objective that contributes to a main objective. Contains specific guidance for completion.
secondary_objective.$comment: Break work into completable steps. Provide guidance referencing documents, examples, standards, or established practices. Each should be achievable in a focused work session.

id.description: Unique identifier across all secondary objectives. Immutable once created.
id.$comment: Start at 1, increment globally across all secondary objectives. Never reuse IDs.

parent_main_id.description: Id of the main objective this secondary serves. Secondaries are a flat list; this links each one to its primary.
parent_main_id.$comment: Optional (backwards-compat: pre-existing logbooks have a flat list with no link). STOP: one parent per secondary — a secondary that serves two primaries is two secondaries. REDIRECT: this is the structural primary->secondary link only; rule/standard inheritance still flows from the parent's scope, not from here. bad: parent_main_id pointing at a non-existent main id, or a secondary advancing primary 1 carrying parent_main_id 2. good: parent_main_id 2 on a secondary whose content advances main objective 2.

created_at.description: UTC timestamp when objective was created (ISO 8601). Immutable.
created_at.$comment: Set once at creation. Never modify.

content.description: Specific verifiable outcome that contributes to task completion. Should be completable in a focused work session.
content.$comment: ONE granular outcome, completable and checkable in a single focused session. STOP: if it contains '+', 'y'/'and', an em-dash, a colon-list, or two verbs, split it into separate secondaries. REDIRECT: the steps to do it (→ this secondary's completion_guide); the rationale (→ the parent main_objective.context). bad: 'Write intro and methods sections, then run them past the editor' (3 concerns) → good: 'Methods section drafted' (the intro and the editor review become their own secondaries).

completion_guide.description: Step-by-step guidance for completing this objective. References documents, examples, standards, or established practices.
completion_guide.$comment: This is WHERE the how lives — one actionable step per array item, each citing a concrete material, section, example, or standard. STOP: one instruction per item; if an item bundles several actions with '+'/'y'/'and', split it into separate items. REDIRECT: restating the outcome (that is content); the rationale/why (that is the parent's context). bad item: 'Write the section well following best practices and get it reviewed' (vague, multi-step, no anchor) → good items: ['Follow the structure of the Chapter 1 introduction', 'Incorporate client feedback from the Jan 15 meeting notes', 'Apply APA 7th edition for all citations'].

function_signatures.description: Concrete function/method signatures this secondary creates or modifies. Real types — no 'any'/'dynamic'/'Object?'. Optional; omit for doc-only or greenfield-no-API secondaries.
function_signatures.$comment: DESIGN SPECIFICATION (design_principle #10). Forces confronting the real API surface at plan time, e.g. 'func (a *App) handlePaste(msg tea.PasteMsg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd)'. Generics are IN scope but MUST declare explicit type-parameter bounds (no unbounded any/dynamic/Object?/interface{} unless architecturally justified — put the justification in the secondary's content). A generic's correctness lives in its instantiations, so test_cases MUST include one edge_case row per concrete instantiation that matters. An unbounded generic with zero instantiation test_cases is the same blind spot as an unconsidered edge case.

test_cases.description: Behavioral scenarios this secondary must satisfy: happy paths + edge cases. DESIGN SPEC, not proof. Optional; populate for code-touching secondaries (design_principle #10, product_rule #10).
test_cases.$comment: test_cases SPECIFY behavior at design time and carry NO verdict. The primary's verification_demonstrations PROVE the suite passes (verdict=pass) by REFERENCE — enumerate once here, prove once there, no duplication (product_rule #10). A secondary touching shared state, async, or sibling handlers with ZERO edge_case:true rows is SUSPECT.

name.description: Identifier of the scenario (what is being tested), not of the implementation. e.g. 'paste during active probe', not 'test_handlePaste_1'.
name.$comment: Name the behavior/condition so the row is meaningful before any code exists.

input.description: Concrete trigger or precondition for the scenario. Optional for cases defined purely by state.
input.$comment: Be concrete: real values/events, e.g. 'PasteMsg arrives while state == probing'. Omit only when the scenario is fully described by name + expected.

expected.description: The behavioral contract: what MUST happen. For edge_case:true rows this is the forcing function — see $comment.
expected.$comment: When edge_case=true and this is EMPTY, the secondary is NOT ready and the logbook is BLOCKED. Filling it requires reading the sibling handlers/code to learn the invariant the new code must preserve. That empty->filled transition is exactly the work that catches relational runtime bugs (design_principle #10).

edge_case.description: THE forcing-function flag. true = boundary / concurrency / error-recovery / cross-handler-interaction case; false = happy path.
edge_case.$comment: Set true for any scenario at a boundary, under concurrency, on an error/recovery path, or that interacts with sibling handlers/shared state. An edge_case:true row with empty 'expected' blocks the logbook until resolved.

status.description: Current state: not_started (pending work), active (in progress), blocked (waiting on external input), achieved (completed), abandoned (cancelled).
status.$comment: Set only ONE secondary objective as 'active' at a time. Work sequentially. Set 'achieved' after verifying content statement is true.
